transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-19 13:42 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO - Mariner), Sofia Diaz (ML Eng), Evan Patel (DevOps)

Summary: quick discovery for PLG quickstart, free credits, how soon can they get to first token, and whether they'll need Dedicated or Private for compliance and latency.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, really excited to chat through your quickstart path and what you guys are trying to build
00:12 Liam O'Connor: yeah thanks Alex, we built Mariner to do real-time maritime analytics and we're looking to add a llm layer for summarization and anomaly explainability. main thing for us is latency at inference and cost since we expect a lot of short requests
00:30 Priya Shah: great, Sofia, Evan you mind if i ask a couple quick q's about current infra and traffic?
00:36 Sofia Diaz: sure, we're on GCP, mostly k8s, using a mix of CPU workers and a couple of GPU nodes for batch training. inference today is a mix of CPU microservices. latency target for the llm endpoints is p95 < 250ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens)
00:58 Priya Shah: ok that helps. could you ballpark qps and token sizes?
01:04 Evan Patel: baseline steady qps like 10-20, spikes to 200 during morning window, average prompt length is short, 30-80 tokens, sometimes we do longer chains for report generation but that's low freq
01:20 Alex Chen: perfect, so sounds like cost-sensitive, low-latency short prompts, a good fit for our hosted API for quick experimentation; dedicated could make sense if you need reserved capacity for spikes or tighter SLOs; private if you need VPC/on-prem or strict data residency
01:38 Liam O'Connor: could you clarify how fast we can get going with the hosted API? time-to-first-token, i.e., get a key, call the api, start seeing results
01:46 Alex Chen: typical plg path is sign up, get free credits (we'll send you 50k tokens to start), quickstart SDKs for node/python, should be able to get first token in <30 minutes if you follow the quickstart. priya can walk through the exact steps
01:58 Priya Shah: yep, we have a quickstart repo, sample prompts and a minimal docker example. i'll send a link. also note streaming responses and function calling are supported, and we have a small sample for embedding + retrieval too
02:15 Sofia Diaz: curious about security — we need SOC2 and audit logs, plus we encrypt data at rest with our KMS. if we go hosted what does that look like?
02:28 Alex Chen: hosted customers are covered by our SOC 2, we can share the whitepaper. data at rest is encrypted and we integrate with customer-managed keys in dedicated/private—hosted has our managed keys but we can provide enterprise options and audit logs in the console. for highest control you can use Redwood Private (VPC) or run the control-plane in your VPC
02:47 Evan Patel: and SSO? we use SAML with okta and need RBAC for team members
02:53 Priya Shah: yes SSO via SAML/SCIM and granular RBAC are supported for enterprise tenants, we'll include docs for setup.
03:01 Liam O'Connor: how does dedicated differ vs hosted on perf and cost? if we move to dedicated does the latency improve a lot?
03:10 Alex Chen: dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and more predictable throughput so your p95 gets more stable; latency improvements depend on model and batch sizes but we often see 15-40% lower tail latency for short prompt workloads because of minimized multi-tenant variability and dedicated kv cache warming. cost wise you pay for reserved capacity so unit cost can be lower if you have steady load, but up-front commit vs pay-as-you-go tradeoff
03:36 Sofia Diaz: any notes about kv cache and batching? our workload has a lot of repeated prefixes across sessions
03:42 Priya Shah: we do automatic prefix/KV caching and continuous batching; for repeated short prefixes you'll see big cost and latency wins. we'll want to tune batching windows per route to hit your p95 target without adding excess latency
03:58 Evan Patel: do you have benchmarks for models on g4/g5 vs triton self host?
04:04 Priya Shah: we publish performance profiles for curated models; we can run a sample benchmark with your sample payload on our infra, that'll be part of the POC scope if you want. note: sometimes Triton numbers look good for throughput but you end up with more ops overhead for orchestration
04:24 Liam O'Connor: what's the billing model for the quickstart — is it per-token, and how do you handle embeddings vs generation?
04:32 Alex Chen: hosted is usage-based per-token and embeddings have separate units. quickstart credits will cover both so you can explore generation, streaming, embeddings. we'll include the pricing sheet.
04:42 Sofia Diaz: data residency — we need EU only storage for some customers. do you have region controls?
04:48 Alex Chen: yes, region pinning and routing policies are supported. for strict residency we'd advise Dedicated or Private in the region; hosted also has region-specific endpoints for many regions but dedicated/private give you stronger isolation
04:59 Evan Patel: if we do a quick POC, what's a reasonable scope and timeline?
05:04 Priya Shah: simple POC: integrate quickstart, run 1k sample queries, measure latency and correctness; run embed+rank flow for retrieval-augmented generation. timeline 2-3 weeks end-to-end assuming we get access to sample data and dev time
05:20 Liam O'Connor: ok that sounds reasonable. question about logs and audit trails — we need long-term retention for compliance
05:27 Alex Chen: we offer extended observability retention as an add-on and can forward logs to your SIEM via connectors, also API audit logs available for enterprise accounts
05:39 Sofia Diaz: any gotchas on private deployment? we may be air-gapped for certain customers
05:44 Priya Shah: private deployments have a customer-controlled control plane, can be on-prem or VPC, we provide a package for air-gapped installs but there is additional operational overhead and licensing. tends to make sense for regulated verticals
05:58 Evan Patel: one last thing — can we bring our own models or must we use Redwood-curated models?
06:03 Alex Chen: you can bring your own model variants in Dedicated and Private, hosting and versioning supported; hosted supports a curated catalog and we're onboarding customer models on request for enterprise plans
06:16 Liam O'Connor: alright, next steps?
06:19 Alex Chen: i'll send the quickstart guide and 50k free credits, priya will follow up to schedule the integration demo and run a benchmark, evan please send expected qps and vpc details. we'll also share SOC2 whitepaper and security FAQ
06:32 Meeting end: thanks everyone

Notes: occasional transcription glitches: "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "key-v cache", product name Redwood sometimes shows as 'Redwood Infer' in notes. Speakers overlapped briefly when discussing dedicated capacity.
